title: One Vehicle, One Enrolment: How Keyturn Host Protection Plan Cover Is Written
content:
Cover under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan is written vehicle by vehicle. A host protects each vehicle separately, so one host may hold as many enrolments as they have vehicles and there is no ceiling on the number. One vehicle may carry only one live enrolment at a time, and an application for a vehicle that already carries a live enrolment is a plan change on that enrolment rather than a second enrolment. Each enrolment carries its own plan, its own deductible and its own claim history, and a claim on one vehicle never moves the deductible or the standing of another.

### The same rule in other words

| Question put to the desk | What the rule gives |
|---|---|
| How many enrolments may one host hold? | As many as the host has vehicles; no ceiling is published. |
| How many live enrolments may one vehicle carry? | One. |
| A host applies again for a vehicle that is already covered | The application is a plan change on the enrolment that already stands, not a second enrolment. |
| A loss is accepted on one of a host's vehicles | The deductible and the standing of the host's other enrolments are untouched by it. |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical host runs four vehicles, three of them enrolled on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan and one not enrolled at all. The three enrolments stand independently: each is written on its own plan, carries its own deductible and keeps its own claim history, and an accepted loss on the first moves nothing on the second or the third.
